payload.question: Will Alaska Ballot Measure 2 (repeal of top-four primaries and RCV) be approved in the November 3, 2026 election?
payload.descriptionMarkdown:
This market resolves **YES** if Alaska Ballot Measure 2 (An Act Restoring Political Party Primaries, Ending Ranked-Choice General Elections, and Repealing Recent Campaign Finance Laws) is **approved by voters at the November 3, 2026 general election** under its official approval rule:

> Majority of votes cast on the proposition (Alaska Const. art. XI §6); effective 90 days after certification.

Only the November 3, 2026 vote counts; earlier votes on similar proposals do not.
YES means voter approval at this election, not that the measure is later implemented.

**What the votes mean (official summary):**
- YES: Yes: repeals top-four primaries and ranked-choice voting, restores party primaries and plurality general elections, and repeals 2020 campaign-finance rules.
- NO: Keeps top-four open primaries, ranked-choice general elections and the 2020 campaign-finance rules.

**Results:** resolves on the result certified by Alaska Division of Elections director / State Review Board; certified under the Lieutenant Governor. It may resolve earlier once official returns or the Associated Press show the outcome cannot change and no recount is pending; if a recount or certified correction changes the outcome before resolution, the certified result controls.

**No vote:** if the measure is removed from the ballot, a court orders its votes not to be counted, or the vote is postponed beyond November 3, 2026, the market resolves N/A.

**Later legal challenges:** resolution follows voter approval as certified. A court later invalidating, enjoining or delaying the measure does not change the resolution.

**Starting probability:** 50% is a starting seed, not a forecast. Basis: unsupported - no recent public poll found (web search 2026-10-03) (the 59-17 Claster poll is from Sept 2020, a different measure).

Official source: https://www.elections.alaska.gov/

This market resolves **YES** if Tennessee Amendment 2 (Proposed amendment to Article II, Section 28 (prohibit state property tax)) is **approved by voters at the November 3, 2026 general election** under its official approval rule:

> Two prongs (Tenn. Const. art. XI §3): (1) more YES than NO; (2) YES votes > half of all votes cast for governor. YES must exceed 50% of total gubernatorial votes; upheld in George v. Hargett (6th Cir. 2018).

Only the November 3, 2026 vote counts; earlier votes on similar proposals do not.
YES means voter approval at this election, not that the measure is later implemented.

**What the votes mean (official summary):**
- YES: Constitution bars any state-level property tax.
- NO: Art. II §28 unchanged; no constitutional ban on a state property tax.

**Results:** resolves on the result certified by Tennessee Secretary of State / State Election Commission (statewide canvass). It may resolve earlier once official returns or the Associated Press show the outcome cannot change and no recount is pending; if a recount or certified correction changes the outcome before resolution, the certified result controls.

**No vote:** if the measure is removed from the ballot, a court orders its votes not to be counted, or the vote is postponed beyond November 3, 2026, the market resolves N/A.

**Later legal challenges:** resolution follows voter approval as certified. A court later invalidating, enjoining or delaying the measure does not change the resolution.

**Starting probability:** 50% is a starting seed, not a forecast. Basis: unsupported - no recent public poll or prior result found (web search 2026-10-03); context: all four 2022 TN amendments passed easily (see TN-amend-1)..

Official source: https://sos.tn.gov/elections/announcements/2026-proposed-constitutional-amendments
